1.explanation:
• docs/callouts.qmd defines and demonstrates the Markdown syntax for Quarto callouts (captions, block types, inline formatting) so you can reproduce the header‐in‐callout scenario.  
• docs/test-singleformat-html.qmd shows how callout captions are correctly processed into HTML (with Markdown formatting) and serves as a reference to compare HTML vs. PDF behavior.  
• docs/test-singleformat-docx.qmd illustrates cross‐format caption handling, helping you verify whether the proposed Lua‐filter change affects other output formats beyond PDF.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that when you author a callout block in Quarto with a Markdown header as the caption — for example “## Text in **strong**, and some `code`” — the PDF‐conversion pipeline uses the raw text of that header literally (no Markdown parsing and no LaTeX‐safe escaping). As a result, inline formatting like **bold** or `code` is lost in the caption, and special characters (commas, percent signs, angle brackets) end up being interpreted as tcolorbox key/value separators or LaTeX operators, triggering compile errors. The callout box itself (a tcolorbox in LaTeX) still renders, but its title bar shows plain text (no bold or code font) and may break the PDF build when it contains commas or `%<-%` sequences.
